title: Winter heat loss does not explain North Atlantic sigma0 26.5 AOU swings; late-winter surface density acting through the BATS class volume gives about half of them (1989-2025)
abstract: Question: North Atlantic AOU on sigma0 26.5 rose 12, fell 10-16 and rose 16-18 umol/kg between the 1997, 2003, 2012 and 2021 A20/A22 occupations. Outcrop-gap ventilation models give only 0.06-0.31 of the 1997-2012 swings (sci:dcfc9b0b, sci:058edf7b), so a second process is needed. We pre-registered one candidate: the renewal volume set by winter air-sea heat loss in the Eighteen Degree Water formation region. Approach: a one-box renewal model, r_t = rbar(1 + b z_t), with z_t the December-March NCEP/NCAR R1 net heat loss over 30-40 N, 75-45 W, fitted on BATS 1989-2009 AOU (J = 4.6 umol/kg/yr) and tested on BATS 2010-2025 and 11 GLODAP line pairs, with 999 year-shuffles. Results: the training fit passed (b > 0, p = 0.016), but the out-of-sample tests failed: BATS 2010-2025 RMSE 14.4 against 10.4 for constant renewal, r = 0.13; A20/A22 swing ratio 0.28; heat loss does not predict the 26.5 class thickness (r = 0.16). Shuffled years did as well (p = 0.17-0.99). Six pre-set variants also failed. Exploratory analyses: the BATS AOU series itself, read at the cruise dates, reproduces the section changes (10 of 11 signs, r = 0.89, slope 1.04), so the swings are basin-coherent. The BATS 26.5 class thickness gives 0.56 of the swings. A class-volume model with 2-3-yr memory forced only by box-mean late-winter surface sigma0 predicts the 2010-2025 thickness (r = 0.91, shuffle p = 0.004) and AOU (r = 0.93), and gives 10 of 11 section signs and 0.44 of the swings (p = 0.007); with heat loss instead it fails (swing 0.08). After 2013 heat loss was near normal while the surface was 1-2.4 s.d. lighter. Conclusion: renewal of the 26.5 class follows late-winter surface density (heat loss plus preconditioning and warming) through the class volume, not the amount of heat loss; this explains about half of the second process. Limitations: the class-volume results are exploratory and chosen among several forcings; one site represents the sections; detrending the density index lowers the swing ratio to 0.30; SST-only density anomaly; all models stay about 10 umol/kg below the observed 2015-2025 BATS AOU.
